info.name: Financial Operating System
info.description:
Personal Financial Operating System — backend API.

**Milestone 2: Categories + Transactions.** (Milestone 1: Foundation + Accounts is also covered below.)

This collection is a living artifact and grows with every implemented endpoint. Folders exist only for features that are actually built.

### Conventions
- All money is sent and received as **JSON strings** (`"32000.00"`), never numbers. A JSON number would be parsed as a float and eventually lose paise.
- Errors are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` with `code`, `field`, `fix` extensions. Switch on `code`, never on `detail`.
- `PATCH` is a partial update: omit a field to leave it unchanged.
- Deletes are **soft**. The row remains; financial history is never destroyed.
- Double-entry postings underneath every transaction are never exposed via the API — the user, and this collection, only ever speaks in transactions.
- `POST /transactions` accepts an optional `Idempotency-Key` header. Repeating the same key with the same body replays the original transaction instead of creating a second one; repeating it with a different body is a 409.

### Setup
1. Start the backend: `cd webapp/backend/finance && ./mvnw spring-boot:run`
2. Run **Health → Health check** to confirm the app and database are up.
3. Run **Accounts → Create bank account**, **Create credit card**, **Create cash account** — each stores an id variable used by later folders.
4. Run **Categories → Create category** — stores `categoryId`.
5. Run requests in **Transactions** — they depend on the account and category ids above.

item.name: Accounts
item.description:
A container of money: bank, cash, credit card, loan or investment.

The opening balance is anchored **per account** with its own date and confidence, because a user often knows one bank's balance exactly and another's only approximately.

`currentBalance` is always derived, never stored: `openingBalance + sum(postings dated after openingAsOf)`. Run requests in **Transactions** and re-run **Get account** here to see it move.

**Required:** `name`, `type`, `openingBalance`, `openingAsOf`.

**`type`** — `BANK` | `CASH` | `CREDIT_CARD` | `LOAN` | `INVESTMENT`. Immutable after creation: changing it would change how every historical figure derived from the account is signed and counted.

item.name: Categories
item.description: A label the user puts on spending, for grouping and comparison. User-editable, system-seeded — see `V2__categories_and_transactions.sql` for the starting set. No budget field: committed vs flexible is handled by Commitments (milestone 4), not a per-category number. See OPEN_QUESTIONS Q2 and ADR-0008.

exec: pm.test('Location header points at the new category', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.include('/api/v1/categories/'));

request.description:
**Required:** `name`, `group`.

**`group`** — `INCOME` | `FLEXIBLE` | `FIXED` | `EVENT` | `NON_SPEND`. Unlike an account's type it carries no compiled behaviour, but it is not purely informational either: `FLEXIBLE` is what This Month's flexible-spending section is computed from, and `INCOME` is enforced against a transaction's direction (an INCOME transaction requires an INCOME category; EXPENSE/REFUND forbid one).

**`parentId`** — optional (V12). Creates this as a **sub-category** of another category. When given, the `group` in the body is ignored and the parent's group is used, so a child always groups with its parent. See "Create sub-category" below.

Uses a name not in the seeded set (`V2__categories_and_transactions.sql`) so this request never collides with the starting categories.

request.description:
Sub-categories are exactly **one level deep** (V12): "Fuel" and "Cab" under "Transport". The parent must be a top-level category.

Note what this request proves: the body asks for `FIXED` and the response comes back `FLEXIBLE` — the parent's group. A child that grouped differently from its parent would have its spend counted in one section of This Month while its parent sat in another, so the group is taken from the parent rather than trusted from the body.

**Rollup:** spend recorded against a sub-category counts toward its parent in `GET /cycles/{id}/flexible-spending`, so adding sub-categories never fragments that view into one line per child.

request.description: Ordered by `displayOrder`, then name. Includes both system-seeded and user-created categories — there is no distinction in how they behave, only in `systemDefined`.

Partial update — omit a field to leave it unchanged.

**`parentId`** — moves this category under another one (V12); it also adopts that parent's group.

**`makeTopLevel`** — `true` promotes a sub-category back out to top level. A separate flag rather than `parentId: null`, because `null` already means "leave unchanged" for every other field on this request and one field cannot mean both.

Archived categories can no longer be assigned to a new transaction (422 `CATEGORY_ARCHIVED`), but every historical transaction that already used it keeps showing it. Run **Unarchive category** before the Transactions folder if you run this collection top-to-bottom.

**Cascades to sub-categories** (V12): archiving a parent archives everything under it, because a child whose parent is gone from every picker has nowhere left to be offered. Unarchiving deliberately does **not** cascade back — which children to restore is a real choice, and guessing "all of them" would resurrect ones that were retired on purpose beforehand.

**Soft delete.** Not run by default in this collection — deleting `categoryId` here would break every later Transactions request that references it. Included for completeness; run it last, deliberately.

**422 `CATEGORY_HAS_CHILDREN`** if the category still has sub-categories. Refused rather than cascaded: a soft-deleted parent with live children would leave those children pointing at a row nothing can reach, which is the orphan ADR-0004 exists to prevent. Archive cascades; delete does not.

item.name: Transactions
item.description:
One ledger entry: date, type, amount, account(s), category. Double-entry postings are generated underneath (see `PostingFactory`) so the same rupee can never be counted twice — the user, and this collection, never sees a posting.

**Five types:** `INCOME` · `EXPENSE` · `TRANSFER` · `INVESTMENT` · `REFUND`. Only `EXPENSE` counts as spending. `TRANSFER`/`INVESTMENT` require a `toAccountId` and forbid a `categoryId`; `INCOME`/`EXPENSE`/`REFUND` require a `categoryId` and forbid a `toAccountId`.

**Run after** Accounts and Categories — every request here depends on `accountId`, `cashAccountId`, `cardAccountId` and `categoryId`.

**`categoryId` includes sub-categories** (V12). request.description:
Gives an **unpaid** occurrence an expected amount — an estimate is fine.

**Why it exists:** a `VARIABLE` mandatory commitment (electricity, petrol) is generated with `expectedAmount: null`, and a mandatory occurrence with an unknown amount holds `GET /position` at `state: INCOMPLETE` (ADR-0006 — never guess). Before this endpoint the only way to give it an amount was `POST …/settle`, which records a payment — so Room was blank from the day the bill was generated until the day it was paid.

When the bill is later settled, `confirmedAmount` is recorded alongside this and the difference is reported as `variance`.

Set `commitmentInstanceId` to an id from `GET /cycles/{id}/commitment-instances` whose `expectedAmount` is null.

request.description:
**One payment pays one bill** (rule 4). `transactionId` here is an expense already linked to a *different* occurrence, so linking it again would count the same money against two bills.

The salary cycle **containing** a date — found, or **created** if it doesn't exist yet.

item.name: Error contract
item.description:
Every error is RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` with our extensions:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | Stable machine identifier. **Switch on this.** |
| `detail` | User-facing sentence, safe to display verbatim |
| `field` | Which request field the error belongs to |
| `fix` | A route the user can follow, when one exists |
| `errors[]` | Per-field messages on validation failures |

Stack traces and internal messages are never returned.
